info.text:
A billion-dollar gain can add $0 to your taxable income.

The income tax generally taxes realized gains, not paper gains: a stock gain is generally taxed only when it's sold.
The Forbes 400 is worth a record $8 trillion in 2026, up $1.4 trillion in a year.
A Sept 2021 White House (CEA/OMB) estimate that counted unrealized gains as income put the 400 wealthiest families' average federal income tax rate at 8.2% for 2010-2018. Cato says paper gains aren't income; the Tax Foundation says the estimate leaves out corporate taxes.
In Moore v. United States (June 2024), the Supreme Court left the realization question open.

Sources: IRS Topic 409; CEA/OMB (Sept 2021); Forbes (Sept 2026); Tax Foundation; Cato; Moore v. US (2024).
News and education, not financial advice.
